hero.title: NiceChunk contracts, live game configuration, and PDA transparency.
hero.subtitle: This page separates the game client's current runtime configuration from contracts that exist in code but are not referenced by that client configuration. A config omission is not an on-chain disable switch. Players can inspect source code, PDA structures, and public devnet accounts from one page.
hero.networkNote: The current game runtime points to Solana devnet through mainnet.json. Mainnet finality and live civilization governance are not claimed here.

directory.title: Current NiceChunk programs and runtime status.
directory.body: The table lists repository contracts, their program IDs, and whether the current game client references them. Client configuration does not by itself prove on-chain deployment or callability.

flow.title: How the current gameplay path touches the chain.

steps.title: Read Genesis Config
steps.body: The client derives GlobalConfig from the core program and reads world seed, chunk size, build limits, NCK mint, and published config hashes.
steps.writes: No user write; derives GlobalConfig PDA
steps.audit: GlobalConfig magic, world seed, hash fields, and runtime program IDs

steps.title: Create Player Profile
steps.body: The player program stores wallet-owned profile data, default attributes, position, equipment slots, and backpack style.
steps.audit: Owner wallet, profile name, position, equipped backpack, and update slot

steps.title: Open Mining Session
steps.body: A player can create an expiry-bearing session authority so repeated mining actions do not require wallet confirmation every block. The caller chooses the expiry, and the program sets no maximum duration or revoke path.
steps.writes: PlayerSession PDA with authority, action mask, expiry, and stored counters
steps.audit: Action mask and expiry are enforced; maxActions and actionCount are stored but not consumed

steps.title: Record Broken Blocks
steps.body: The chunk program verifies the generated single block, then writes a compact 3-byte broken-block record into the chunk-broken PDA.
steps.writes: ChunkBrokenState record under the Chunk program
steps.audit: Packed broken-block records, minY, count/capacity, and block proof assumptions

steps.title: Publish Player Buildings
steps.body: The Building program checks PlayerSession signer binding and expiry, but every current player branch requests BREAK_BLOCK rather than a distinct build permission. It indexes chunks and finalizes NCM3 manifests; a separate restricted-wallet path forwards Guardian blueprint metadata without checking a manifest.
steps.audit: Foundation footprint, revision state, shard bitmap, NCM3 hash, and Guardian blueprint hash

steps.title: Append Resources
steps.body: The backpack program is prepared to append mined resource records after session validation. It is the inventory-side bridge for the mining loop.
steps.writes: Backpack slot append or mutation through authorized program signer
steps.audit: Backpack owner, itemCount, slot payload, durability, material/item identity

steps.title: Smelt Resources Into Items
steps.body: The Smelting program reads a caller-selected program-owned RecipeTable, matches selected Backpack input and fuel slots to that table, removes them, and appends table-derived outputs through the smelting-authority PDA. It does not enforce a canonical table or authority.
steps.writes: RecipeTable read plus Backpack remove/append through smelting authority
steps.audit: Selected table ID and authority provenance, recipe IDs, heat tiers, input/output volumes, disabled recipes, and output slot evidence

steps.title: List Backpack Items
steps.body: The marketplace reads the selected 80-byte slot from the seller Backpack PDA, removes that slot, and escrows the full slot snapshot inside the Listing PDA.
steps.audit: Seller, buyer, currency, price, escrow state, and original slot snapshot

steps.title: Settle Market Orders
steps.body: A buyer pays in NCK or SOL, the program routes a 1% market fee to treasury, and the escrowed Backpack slot bytes are delivered through the market authority. If the slot references a BlueprintItem, its separate owner field is not updated.
steps.writes: Listing settlement and buyer Backpack delivery
steps.audit: Treasury fee routing, payment mint/native flag, settled slot, and final listing state

programs.name: NiceChunk Genesis Core
programs.role: One-time world configuration and NCK mint validation under the current program logic.
programs.summary: Under the current Core logic, initialize_global_config writes the GlobalConfig PDA once from compiled genesis parameters. The current dispatcher has no config-update or admin branch, but source code alone does not prove that the deployed program upgrade authority is closed.
instructions: Only the exact one-byte payload [0] is accepted; every other discriminator is invalid.
Validates SPL Token mint layout, decimals, initialized flag, genesis supply, disabled mint authority, and disabled freeze authority.
Creates or allocates the GlobalConfig PDA safely even if the PDA was pre-funded with dust lamports.
storage: World ID and 32-byte world seed.
Terrain, resource rule, and client world config hashes.
NCK mint, decimals, genesis supply, and development wallet.
Chunk size, section height, build limits, max terrain height, sea level, cooldowns, and guardian settings.
notes: The current program exposes no config update or admin instruction, but the source does not prove that the deployed program upgrade authority has been closed.
Future crafting, inventory, chunk state, world knowledge, and reputation systems belong in separate programs or future modules after PDA specs are finalized.
Devnet and testnet must use their own NCK mint; the mainnet mint should not be reused on development clusters.

programs.name: NiceChunk Player
programs.role: Wallet-owned player profile, position, equipment slots, backpack style, and mining session authority.
programs.summary: The Player program creates a wallet-bound profile and an expiry-bearing session authority. Consumers enforce signer binding, action mask, and expiry, but the caller may choose an arbitrarily distant expiry and there is no revoke/close path or enforced action counter.
instructions: All other player tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: Owner wallet, GlobalConfig address, world ID, bump, and timestamps.
Base attributes: health, energy, stamina, mining power, build power, and defense.
Current position and nine equipment slots.
Session authority, allowed action bitmask, expiration time, and stored maxActions/actionCount fields.
notes: The profile is public state. It stores the equipped backpack public key, while private backpack contents are loaded separately when the player opens inventory flows.
The current session model is used to reduce repeated wallet prompts during mining.

Current consumers enforce signer binding, expiration, and allowed action flags. They do not check or increment maxActions/actionCount, impose a maximum session duration, or provide revoke/close; refreshing an existing session requires both the owner and existing session authority to sign.

programs.name: NiceChunk Chunk
programs.role: Verifies generated single blocks and records compact broken-block state per chunk.
programs.accountSize: ChunkBrokenState: 16-byte header + 3 bytes per capacity record; rule and foundation indexes use separate layouts
programs.summary: The chunk program uses the current optimized mining path. For mining, the player submits one world block coordinate. The program derives the chunk, verifies the generated block, rejects air/water/bedrock or already-mined positions, and appends a compressed broken-block record.
instructions: Legacy chunk tags 0-4 are not accepted by the current dispatcher.
storage: ChunkBrokenState stores a 16-byte header and 3-byte mined-block records; the current dispatcher has no legacy ChunkState branch.
ResourceDropTable, SurfaceDecorationTable, and FoundationChunk accounts keep rule and occupied-foundation evidence in separate PDA families.
A record packs local x, local z, and y offset. Capacity starts at 64, grows by 64, and caps at 2,048 records.
GlobalConfig world seed, chunk size, build height, max terrain height, and sea level are used for generated block verification.
notes: This is the current mining write path used by the browser client.
Legacy Chunk tags 0-4 are rejected by the current dispatcher; no MagicBlock delegation instruction is active in this crate.
Backpack resource settlement is intentionally separate so mining state and inventory state can evolve independently.

pdaAccounts.purpose: Sparse record of generated blocks broken by players.

pdaAccounts.purpose: Bounded extra-drop rules for rewarded mining.

programs.name: NiceChunk Unified Game Router
programs.role: Consumes a one-byte namespace envelope and forwards the remaining payload to Backpack, Chunk, Smelting, or Market logic compiled into one executable.
programs.sdk: No standalone SDK; callers prepend a namespace byte to the child-module payload.
programs.summary: The unified Game program dispatches namespace 1 to Backpack, 2 to Chunk, 3 to Smelting, and 4 to Market, passing the same incoming program ID into the selected child processor. public/mainnet.json currently aliases Backpack, Market, and Smelting to this executable while Chunk remains separately routed. The selected cluster feature must propagate to every child crate so mint and cluster constants cannot silently remain on Devnet in a testnet or mainnet build.
instructions: An empty payload or any other namespace returns InvalidInstruction (custom error 6600).
pdaSeeds: No router-owned seed domain; unified child PDAs derive under the incoming Game program ID.
storage: The router owns no separate state layout and writes only through the selected child module.
The first byte is removed before the child module reads its own instruction discriminator.
notes: Wire format is [namespace, childTag, childPayload...], not the standalone child payload by itself.
Equal runtime IDs for logical labels are routing aliases, not proof of independent deployments.
Devnet, testnet, and mainnet features forward to every routed child dependency; conflicting or missing cluster selection is rejected at compile time.

programs.name: NiceChunk Building
programs.kind: Build sites, NCM3 building manifests, and Guardian blueprint publishing
programs.role: Owns BuildSite v2 accounts, chunk indexing, building manifests, upload shards, resize flow, and Guardian blueprint publishing authority.
programs.accountSize: BuildSite: 160 bytes; legacy BuildSite: 136 bytes; BuildingManifest: 160 bytes; BuildingShard: 64 + payload bytes
programs.summary: The Building program creates and resizes BuildSite accounts, registers occupied chunks, stages and finalizes NCM3 uploads, migrates legacy sites, and publishes Guardian blueprint metadata. Its session guard checks signer binding and expiry but currently requests BREAK_BLOCK for every player branch rather than a distinct build permission.
instructions: All other building tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: BuildSite stores owner, global config, foundation ID, footprint, surface Y, active and pending revisions, indexed chunk counters, staged resize dimensions, and update slots.
BuildingManifest stores owner, global config, foundation ID, revision, payload length, expected NCM3 hash, dimensions, rotation, offsets, shard count, uploaded bitmap, and status.
BuildingShard stores one bounded payload segment for an NCM3 building upload, with uploaded length and payload bytes after the 64-byte header.
notes: PlayerSession-gated Building branches require a matching PlayerProfile and live session, but request the BREAK_BLOCK bit instead of the defined PLACE_BLOCK bit; the restricted-publisher blueprint branch has no PlayerSession gate.
A BuildingManifest only becomes active after all shards are written, the payload hash matches, and the NCM3 dimensions fit the BuildSite footprint and world height limits.

Guardian blueprint publication is restricted to the treasury or configured publisher wallet and calls Guardian through a Building PDA, but tag 8 does not read a BuildingManifest or prove that the submitted summary matches a finalized building.
The 136-byte legacy BuildSite layout is still decoded so deployed foundations can be migrated safely.

programs.name: NiceChunk Guardian Registry
programs.role: Registers NCK-staked Guardian regions with operator endpoints and blueprint metadata; proof and settlement branches are not live in V2.
programs.summary: The Guardian program records regional service endpoints and accepts an NCK registration transfer into the treasury token account. Retired proof and settlement tags are rejected; V2 has no proof, slash, deregistration, stake exit/refund, or structured event-emission path.
instructions: Tags 3 and 4 are retired/unassigned and are rejected by the current process_instruction tests.
storage: Registry stores GlobalConfig, NCK mint, treasury token account, active count, and genesis flag.
Region stores treasury ownership, the Guardian operator, endpoint, stake, legacy proof/penalty fields, and chain-committed blueprint hash, revision, and record count.
Region size is 100 by 100 chunks. Registration requires a 100,000 NCK treasury payment at 6 decimals.
The layout retains proof interval, penalty, and slash fields, but the current dispatcher has no proof, settlement, slash, deregistration, refund, or stake-reclaim instruction.
notes: The current web Guardian page reads this registry and region PDA data from devnet.

Only the stored Guardian operator can update the endpoint. The fixed treasury wallet can replace the operator in one transaction without operator acceptance, a timelock, or an on-chain governance vote; the restricted Building publisher path updates blueprint metadata.

The registration transfer goes to the treasury token account. V2 has no deregistration, stake reclaim, refund, slash, or structured event instruction; reviewers must use transaction history and account diffs.

programs.name: NiceChunk Backpack
programs.kind: Inventory slot layer for blocks, resources, and items
programs.role: Creates player backpacks, stores block-resource and item slots, removes selected slots, and accepts marketplace or smelting-authorized delivery.
programs.summary: The Backpack program stores fixed 80-byte resource and item slots and supports mining, smelting, forging, equipment, and marketplace paths. A session carrying BREAK_BLOCK can call tag 2 to remove any selected slot index; tag 8 validates NCF1 bytes and material requirements but does not validate a BlueprintItem or issuer record.
instructions: All other backpack tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: Backpack header stores backpack ID, owner, capacity, item count, state, placement fields, timestamps, and flags.
Default capacity is 50 slots. Max capacity is 99 slots.
Each v3 BackpackSlotRecord is 80 bytes: kind, category, flags, quantity, resource coordinate, item code, item ID, item PDA, volume, durability, grade, item level, quality, and metadata.
Slot kind 1 stores block resources. Slot kind 2 stores item/material records such as smelted outputs or forged outputs.
The decoder only accepts the current v3 account layout.
notes: Backpack contents are separate from public player profile display; the player profile stores only the equipped backpack public key.
The marketplace program can escrow or deliver backpack resources through the market-authority PDA.

The smelting program can append material or item outputs through the smelting-authority PDA; output trust still depends on the selected RecipeTable provenance because execution does not enforce a canonical table.
Direct player appends remain restricted to validated mining sessions for block resources, but tag 2 also lets a BREAK_BLOCK session remove any selected Backpack slot, including an item slot.

pdaAccounts.name: Backpack
pdaAccounts.purpose: Wallet-owned inventory PDA for block resources and item references.
fields: up to 99 slot records with block resource or item reference

programs.name: NiceChunk Smelting
programs.kind: Recipe table and backpack item creation layer
programs.role: Stores smelting recipe tables, consumes selected backpack resources and fuels, and appends material or item outputs back into the backpack.
programs.summary: The smelting program separates recipe authority from backpack storage. A recipe table PDA stores up to 10 recipes, each with up to 8 input slots and 4 output slots. Execution validates selected Backpack inputs and fuel, but accepts any RecipeTable owned by this program; table ID and authority provenance must therefore be verified separately before trusting its outputs.
instructions: execute_smelting supports input indexes, fuel indexes, and a batch multiplier.
storage: RecipeTable stores table ID, authority, recipe count, timestamps, and fixed-size recipe records.
Each RecipeRecord stores recipe ID, enabled flag, minimum heat tier, input count, output count, up to 8 input BackpackSlot records, up to 4 output BackpackSlot records, and updated slot.
BackpackSlot records support block resources and item/material outputs.
Recipe table authority can upsert recipes and can transfer authority in one step to any pubkey, including the default pubkey, with no acceptance or recovery step.
notes: Any signer can initialize an unused table ID and becomes that RecipeTable authority; a Civilization receipt can also patch a target table.
Execution validates backpack ownership, recipe matching, input slots, fuel slots, and batch multiplier before consuming inventory.
The smelting-authority PDA gates Backpack writes, but it does not make the selected RecipeTable canonical or trusted.

pdaAccounts.name: RecipeTable
pdaAccounts.purpose: Authority-owned smelting recipe table used by the smelting program.
fields: each recipe stores heat tier, input slots, output slots and updatedSlot

pdaAccounts.name: SmeltingAuthority
pdaAccounts.purpose: Program signer used to append outputs that match the caller-selected RecipeTable; it does not establish table provenance or canonicality.

programs.name: NiceChunk Marketplace
programs.role: Creates listings from seller Backpack PDA slots, escrows the full 80-byte slot, settles NCK or SOL payment, and restores or delivers inventory on cancel or purchase.
programs.summary: The Marketplace program escrows an existing 80-byte Backpack slot snapshot and restores or delivers those slot bytes on cancel or purchase. For BlueprintItem slots, this moves the Backpack record only; it does not update the separate BlueprintItem owner field.
instructions: Create listing only accepts listingId, currency, sourceType, sourceIndex, and price; item parameters are read from the Backpack PDA.
Cancellation and purchase write the Listing-owned 80-byte slot back into the target Backpack through the market-authority PDA.
Payment supports NCK and SOL with a 1% market fee.
storage: Listing stores seller wallet, listing ID, currency, source type/index, price, the full source slot snapshot, timestamps, buyer, and final settlement fields.
The source slot is copied from Backpack v3 slot data during create_listing; category, quantity, itemCode, durability, grade, itemLevel, and quality are never accepted from user payload.
A purchased listing remains a sold settlement record. A canceled listing restores the escrowed slot, zeroes its data, and refunds listing lamports to the seller.
notes: Only the listing seller can cancel an active listing.
Buyers cannot purchase their own listings.
Only the marketplace PDA can restore or deliver escrowed slots through the backpack program.
Treasury fee is 1% of the listing price in the chosen currency.
Marketplace settlement transfers Backpack slot bytes only and does not update a referenced BlueprintItem account owner.

pdaAccounts.name: MarketplaceAuthority
pdaAccounts.purpose: Program signer for escrow restore, delivery, and settlement authority boundaries.
fields: Does not custody player wallets outside explicit instructions

programs.name: NiceChunk Civilization
programs.status: Implemented / not in current client config
programs.role: Publishes rulebooks, signatures, tallies, execution receipts, Civilization Value snapshots, and citizen power accounts.
programs.magic: NCKCVR01 / NCKCVS01 / NCKCVT01 / NCKCVE01 / NCKCVP01 / NCKCVC01
programs.accountSize: RuleBook: 320; Signature: 136; Tally: 128; Receipt: 128; PowerSnapshot: 128; CitizenPower: 144 bytes
programs.summary: The Civilization program exists in the repository and SDK, but it is not part of the current mainnet.json game runtime configuration yet. It records proposals, signatures, caller-supplied tallies, execution receipts, and authority-settled power. The current code has no enforced voting window and does not prove that every available signature was included in a tally.
instructions: All other civilization tags return InvalidInstruction.
storage: RuleBook stores hashes, target program/PDA, threshold, risk level, total power, required power, and tally counters.
RuleSignature stores signer side and settled snapshot power.
PowerSnapshot stores authority-signed total active power, epoch fields, hash, and expiresAt; tally does not compare the stored epoch range with Clock.
CitizenPower stores a power amount bound to one snapshot. expiresAt is checked during settlement and signing, but tally does not re-check signature age, expiry, or epoch fields.
notes: The current game client does not submit Civilization instructions because mainnet.json omits its program ID; this client-side omission does not disable direct calls if the program is deployed.
Civilization Value cannot be self-reported; power snapshots and citizen power settlement require the configured authority signer.
Players can inspect the intended PDA structure here, but deployment and on-chain program authority must be verified separately before treating any records as live.

civilization-rule-tally.visible: Agree, reject, abstain, challenge power, required power, and threshold result.
civilization-rule-tally.trust: Shows the threshold result for the signature accounts supplied by the finalizer; it does not prove every available signature was counted.

civilization-execution-receipt.title: Civilization execution receipts
civilization-execution-receipt.body: Account recording rule execution or acknowledgement.
civilization-execution-receipt.visible: RuleBook, executor, executed slot, and timestamp.
civilization-execution-receipt.trust: Binds a receipt to its RuleBook and stored threshold result; it does not prove that all signatures were counted or that a voting window elapsed.

civilization-power-snapshot.title: Civilization Value snapshots
civilization-power-snapshot.visible: Authority, snapshot hash, total active power, window, and expiry.
civilization-power-snapshot.trust: Shows authority-declared power, epoch fields, and expiry; the current tally path does not enforce the stored epoch window against Clock.

civilization-citizen-power.title: CitizenPower accounts
civilization-citizen-power.body: One citizen power amount bound to a snapshot; the epoch range is stored metadata rather than an enforced tally window.
civilization-citizen-power.visible: Citizen, snapshot, power, settled slot, and expiry.
civilization-citizen-power.trust: Shows settled signer power used at signature time; finalization does not re-check expiry or include every available signature automatically.

transparency.title: Players can audit the world from contract code to public PDA state.
transparency.body: NiceChunk treats public state as part of the game interface. Players should be able to inspect who exists, which backpacks and listings exist, what recipes are active, which regions serve realtime play, and which rules or accounts are still only planned.

cards.title: Players are public account records, not hidden rows in a private database.
cards.body: PlayerProfile and PlayerSession PDAs expose the wallet, position, equipped backpack pointer, session authority, enforced action mask and expiry, and stored counter fields that current consumers do not enforce.
points: Enforced session mask/expiry and non-enforced counter fields are distinguishable.

cards.title: Backpacks and market listings are readable storage objects.
cards.body: Backpack and MarketplaceListing accounts show item counts, Backpack owners, states, prices, and safe sample slots. This traces slot-byte movement, but Marketplace does not update a referenced BlueprintItem.owner field.
points: Forged items surface through Backpack item slots.

cards.title: Terrain and mining state are tied to verifiable world config.
cards.body: GlobalConfig fixes the world seed and config hashes, while ChunkBrokenState and ResourceDropTable expose what has been mined and which extra-drop rules exist.
points: World seed and hashes are public.
Broken-block records are compact but readable.
Drop tables are bounded PDA data.

cards.title: Civilization records require separate deployment and state verification.
cards.body: The Civilization contract defines rulebooks, signatures, caller-supplied tallies, receipts, and Civilization Value accounts. Its ID is absent from the current client config, which does not itself disable a deployed program.
points: Client runtime config and on-chain availability are separate.
Rule targets must point to inspectable PDAs.

map.audit: Read PlayerProfile accounts to see wallets, positions, equipment slots, and equipped backpack pointers.
Read Backpack accounts to inspect owners, capacity, item counts, block resources, and item/material slots.
Read forged records from Backpack item slots without inventing a separate live forging program.
Read RecipeTable accounts to inspect active recipe tables, heat tiers, input counts, output counts, and update slots.
Read BuildSite, BuildingManifest, and BuildingShard accounts to inspect foundation footprints, upload progress, active revisions, and NCM3 payload metadata.
Read GuardianRegion and GuardianRegistry accounts to audit operator, endpoint, stake, blueprint revision, and dormant proof/penalty fields.
Read MarketplaceListing accounts to inspect seller, buyer, price, currency, escrowed slot, state, and settlement slots.
Read RuleBook, signature, tally, receipt, power snapshot, and citizen power accounts to inspect the governance path.

runtime.title: What the game client is actually configured to use now.
runtime.body: This section reads the public mainnet.json runtime index and separates programs referenced by the current game client from contracts that exist in code. Omission from this file is not an on-chain disable switch.

config.label: Runtime index
config.title: The game still uses the public runtime config.
config.body: mainnet.json reports cluster {cluster} and app version {version}. It remains the high-frequency game config, not a website i18n bundle.

programs.label: Active programs
programs.title: Programs currently referenced by the game client.
programs.body: These are the client routing IDs currently supplied by mainnet.json. They select executables for this build; by themselves they do not prove deployed ELF identity, ProgramData upgrade authority, or independent deployments for logical module labels.

alias.label: Shared game program
alias.title: Some modules currently point to the same program ID.
alias.body: This reflects the current client configuration: backpack, smelting, and market map to one shared executable ID. Chunk has its own configured ID, and configuration alone does not prove deployment state.

civilization.label: Civilization
civilization.title: Civilization exists in code but is not referenced by the current game client.
civilization.bodyConfigured: The Civilization program is present in the runtime configuration.
civilization.bodyGated: The Civilization program is documented and decodable here, but it is not in the current mainnet.json runtime config. That omission alone neither proves it is undeployed nor prevents direct calls to a deployed program.

auditMatrix.title: What an external reviewer should verify for each contract surface.
auditMatrix.body: This matrix ties each program to the authority gate, PDA evidence, live proof, and current boundary that can be checked without trusting a private server.

rows.intent: Proves that world constants and program IDs are derived from a public configuration account.
rows.authority: The current Core dispatcher writes GlobalConfig once and exposes no update branch; deployed program upgrade authority must be verified separately.
rows.evidence: GlobalConfig PDA, config hash fields, NCK mint, world seed, chunk dimensions, Guardian parameters.
rows.live: Compare /mainnet.json with the GlobalConfig PDA in the RPC browser.
rows.boundary: Core does not mint items, mutate terrain, update inventory, or execute governance.

rows.intent: Shows which wallet owns a public player profile and which expiry-bearing session may submit masked actions; no maximum duration or revoke path is enforced.
rows.authority: Owner wallet initializes profile/session state; consumers enforce the session signer, action mask, and expiry, but not maxActions/actionCount.
rows.evidence: PlayerProfile, PlayerSession, PlayerAppearance, and equipment PDA records.
rows.live: Read player-profile and player-session groups, then match owner, session authority, and update slot.
rows.boundary: A cached browser wallet is not proof of control; the PDA owner and signatures are the trust boundary.

rows.intent: Separates generated terrain proof from the sparse record of blocks that have actually been mined.
rows.authority: Chunk logic recomputes the target block from GlobalConfig and rejects invalid, protected, or already broken blocks.
rows.evidence: ChunkBrokenState packed records, ResourceDropTable, SurfaceDecorationTable, minY, count, and capacity.
rows.live: Scan ChunkBrokenState and ResourceDropTable accounts for the target world and chunk coordinates.
rows.boundary: The program stores sparse mutations, not the full terrain; inventory settlement is handled by Backpack.

rows.intent: Makes the one-byte namespace envelope and the address domain used by compiled child processors explicit.
rows.authority: Only namespaces 1-4 are accepted. The router removes that byte and passes the incoming Game program ID, accounts, and remaining child payload into Backpack, Chunk, Smelting, or Market logic.
rows.evidence: The router owns no account state; routed child PDA derivation and account ownership checks use the incoming Game program ID.
rows.live: Compare the current mainnet.json aliases (Backpack, Market, and Smelting to Game; Chunk standalone) with the exact built and deployed ELF.
rows.boundary: Configuration and source do not prove the deployed ProgramData or upgrade authority, and logical aliases are not independent deployments.

rows.intent: Shows whether a player-owned foundation and uploaded NCM3 building payload were validated before publication.
rows.authority: PlayerProfile and PlayerSession gate BuildSite writes, but current Building branches request BREAK_BLOCK rather than the defined PLACE_BLOCK action bit.
rows.evidence: BuildSite, BuildingManifest, BuildingShard, chunk authority PDA, Guardian blueprint authority PDA.
rows.live: Inspect build-site, building-manifest, and building-shard accounts; compare footprint, revision, hash, dimensions, and shard bitmap.
rows.boundary: A manifest only becomes active after every shard is present and the payload hash and fit checks pass.

rows.intent: Lets a reviewer check which realtime regions exist and which operator endpoint is publicly registered.
rows.authority: The fixed treasury initializes registry state and can rotate an operator without acceptance; the current operator can update only the endpoint.
rows.evidence: GuardianRegistry and GuardianRegion records with owner, operator, endpoint, proof counters, stake, and blueprint metadata.
rows.live: Scan guardian-registry and guardian-region accounts, then compare endpoint, operator, stake, blueprint revision, and legacy proof fields.
rows.boundary: Proof/settlement tags are retired, stake has no exit/refund/slash path, stored counters do not prove liveness, and the program emits no structured lifecycle events.

rows.intent: Keeps mined resources, item references, and custody transfers visible as fixed-size slot records.
rows.authority: Owner and program-PDA paths mutate slots, and Backpack tag 2 also accepts a BREAK_BLOCK session that may remove any selected slot index.
rows.evidence: Backpack PDA, itemCount, 80-byte slot payloads, source coordinates, material or item identity, durability.
rows.live: Scan backpack accounts and verify itemCount, slot type, material IDs, item hashes, and source coordinates.
rows.boundary: Slot custody is explicit, but tag 8 does not validate BlueprintItem issuer evidence and Marketplace does not update a referenced BlueprintItem owner.

rows.intent: Shows which public recipe table drove material conversion; public state alone does not make that table canonical.
rows.authority: Any signer can initialize an unused table ID and become its authority; the smelting PDA appends outputs from any program-owned table selected at execution.
rows.evidence: RecipeTable records, recipe IDs, heat tiers, input and output volumes, disabled recipe flags.
rows.live: Read recipe-table accounts and compare them with public/rules/smelting-rules.json and Backpack output slots.
rows.boundary: Execution checks program ownership but no canonical table allowlist or trusted authority, so reviewers must verify table ID, authority, and recipe provenance.

rows.intent: Shows whether a listed asset is a concrete Backpack slot snapshot and how settlement returns or delivers it.
rows.authority: Seller signs the listing; market authority escrows, cancels, or delivers the exact slot snapshot.
rows.evidence: MarketplaceListing, seller, buyer, currency, price, escrowed slot bytes, settlement status.
rows.live: Scan market-listing accounts and compare original slot snapshot, buyer, fee routing, and final state.
rows.boundary: The Listing is a slot-byte escrow record, not proof of an off-chain orderbook or transfer of a referenced BlueprintItem account owner.

rows.intent: Makes rule proposals, signatures, power snapshots, caller-supplied tallies, and execution receipts auditable without treating them as complete or windowed approval.
rows.authority: A fixed power authority settles power; any payer may propose, finalize a caller-supplied signature subset, and execute after that subset's recorded threshold result passes.
rows.evidence: RuleBook, RuleSignature, RuleTally, ExecutionReceipt, PowerSnapshot, CitizenPower.
rows.live: Use the Civilization PDA groups to inspect records if the program is deployed. The current mainnet.json omission describes client wiring and does not block direct on-chain submission.
rows.boundary: Target adapters bind governable writes, but proposal threshold may be as low as 1 bps, no voting window is enforced, and a tally need not include every available signature.

logic.title: Understand the contracts as a connected trust graph.
logic.body: Each map shows the actor, program boundary, PDA evidence, and public verification surface. The goal is to explain what the contracts actually protect before a reader opens the code or RPC browser.

diagrams.title: Wallet intent becomes public state only through narrow program gates.
diagrams.body: The client can prepare instructions, but durable game state appears only after the wallet, session authority, and program checks agree on the same GlobalConfig and owner relationship.

nodes.label: Player wallet
nodes.detail: Owns profile creation and co-signs refresh of an existing session with that session authority; also signs owner-gated backpack and market actions.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Repeats action-mask-approved gameplay until a caller-chosen expiry; there is no maximum duration, revoke path, or enforced action counter.

nodes.label: Genesis Core
nodes.detail: Writes the world seed, hashes, NCK mint, and bounds once under current Core logic; executable upgrade authority is separate evidence.

nodes.label: Player Program
nodes.detail: Validates owner/profile/session relationships before gameplay instructions can rely on identity.

nodes.label: GlobalConfig
nodes.detail: A one-time runtime anchor under current Core logic; deployed executable and upgrade authority remain separate evidence.

nodes.label: PlayerProfile
nodes.detail: Public profile record with owner, position, equipment slots, backpack pointer, and forge progress.

nodes.label: PlayerSession
nodes.detail: Binds wallet and session authority to an action mask and expiry; maxActions/actionCount are stored but not enforced.

nodes.label: Game client
nodes.detail: Reads mainnet.json, derives PDAs, and submits only the instructions the visible state allows.

nodes.label: PDA browser
nodes.detail: Reads program accounts from devnet RPC and decodes known account layouts in this page.

evidence: Counter fields are public but not enforced

diagrams.title: Generated terrain, broken blocks, and rewards are separate audit surfaces.
diagrams.body: Chunk state does not store the whole world. It stores compact deltas against deterministic terrain plus bounded rule tables for resource and surface decoration behavior.

nodes.label: Mine block intent
nodes.detail: A wallet or session authority declares the world coordinate and expected generated block.

nodes.label: Foundation intent
nodes.detail: The player claims a bounded footprint that later protects occupied chunks from incompatible writes.

nodes.label: Chunk verifier
nodes.detail: Recomputes generated block identity from GlobalConfig before accepting a broken-block write.

nodes.label: Chunk authority PDA
nodes.detail: Lets related programs coordinate chunk occupancy without giving them unrestricted write access.

nodes.label: ChunkBrokenState
nodes.detail: Stores compact 3-byte records for blocks that differ from generated terrain.

nodes.label: FoundationChunk
nodes.detail: Indexes which player foundations occupy each chunk so building and mining can reason about conflicts.

nodes.label: ResourceDropTable
nodes.detail: Publishes extra-drop rules without embedding mutable probabilities in client-only code.

nodes.label: SurfaceDecorationTable
nodes.detail: Keeps surface decoration sync auditable against deterministic terrain faces.

diagrams.title: A player building is staged and hash-checked, while Guardian blueprint metadata follows a separate, non-manifest-verified path.
diagrams.body: The Building program separates footprint ownership, upload progress, final manifest hash, chunk registration, and Guardian blueprint publication so each risk has a specific PDA witness.

nodes.label: Player session
nodes.detail: Building checks the profile, signer, and expiry, but every current branch requests BREAK_BLOCK rather than a distinct build permission.

nodes.label: NCM3 payload
nodes.detail: The client shards a building payload, commits the expected hash, and uploads bounded segments.

nodes.label: Building Program
nodes.detail: Owns BuildSite v2, upload shards, manifest finalization, resize state, and legacy migration.

nodes.label: Blueprint authority
nodes.detail: A restricted wallet invokes a program-derived signer to publish blueprint metadata; the path does not compare it with a finalized BuildingManifest.

nodes.label: BuildSite
nodes.detail: Stores owner, footprint, active/pending revisions, staged resize dimensions, and chunk counts.

nodes.label: BuildingManifest
nodes.detail: Stores expected hash, NCM dimensions, rotation, offsets, shard bitmap, and active/uploading status.

nodes.label: BuildingShard
nodes.detail: Stores one bounded piece of the upload so finalization can reconstruct and verify the payload hash.

nodes.label: Chunk occupancy index
nodes.detail: Building registration updates chunk occupancy through the chunk authority boundary.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion blueprint
nodes.detail: Guardian regions store blueprint hash, revision, and record count for realtime serving.

diagrams.title: Backpack slot bytes remain inspectable across smelting and marketplace paths.
diagrams.body: Backpack and Listing accounts expose slot-byte changes, but this is slot-level evidence: a BREAK_BLOCK session can remove any selected slot, and Marketplace does not transfer a referenced BlueprintItem owner field.

nodes.label: Backpack owner
nodes.detail: Starts backpack creation, item use, smelting selection, listing, cancellation, or purchase delivery.

nodes.label: Buyer / seller
nodes.detail: Market settlement binds payment, seller, buyer, price, currency, and escrowed slot state.

nodes.label: Backpack Program
nodes.detail: Owns slot creation, removal, and authorized delivery from other programs.

nodes.label: Smelting Program
nodes.detail: Reads a caller-selected program-owned RecipeTable, consumes matching resources/fuels, and appends table-derived outputs without canonical-table enforcement.

nodes.label: Market Program
nodes.detail: Escrows a selected backpack slot and releases it on cancel or settlement.

nodes.label: Backpack
nodes.detail: Stores block resources, material slots, forged item refs, durability, grade, and item identity.

nodes.label: RecipeTable
nodes.detail: Stores heat, inputs, outputs, disabled flags, and per-output volume for recipes.

nodes.label: MarketplaceListing
nodes.detail: Stores seller, buyer, state, price, currency, and the full escrowed backpack slot.

nodes.label: Forged item view
nodes.detail: The PDA browser derives forged outputs from Backpack item slots instead of pretending a separate live forging program exists.

nodes.label: Treasury fee route
nodes.detail: Market settlement routes configured fees while preserving buyer delivery and seller proceeds in account state.

evidence: Slot snapshots preserve bytes, not external BlueprintItem ownership

diagrams.title: Rule execution records signatures, a caller-supplied tally, a receipt, and power accounts.
diagrams.body: These PDAs are independently decodable, but they do not prove a complete or windowed vote: the author may choose a 1 bps threshold and the finalizer chooses which signature accounts to include.

nodes.label: Rule author
nodes.detail: Publishes a rulebook with target program, target PDA, payload hash, and required power.

nodes.label: Citizen signer
nodes.detail: Signs agree, reject, abstain, or challenge against the exact RuleBook and settled power snapshot.

nodes.label: Civilization Program
nodes.detail: Publishes rulebooks, signatures, tallies, receipts, power snapshots, and citizen power records.

nodes.label: Target adapter authority
nodes.detail: Binds execution of the stored threshold result to the target program; it does not establish that the tally was complete or windowed.

nodes.label: RuleBook
nodes.detail: Proposal record with target, payload hash, author-selected threshold, and power snapshot hash; RuleBook has no voting-expiry field.

nodes.label: RuleSignature
nodes.detail: One signer-side record that binds vote side and power to the exact rulebook.

nodes.label: RuleTally / Receipt
nodes.detail: Aggregates only the signature accounts supplied by the finalizer and records whether that subset met the stored threshold.

nodes.label: PowerSnapshot
nodes.detail: Authority-settled total active power used to validate impossible signature sets.

nodes.label: CitizenPower
nodes.detail: Per-citizen power whose expiry is checked when signing; tally can later count the stored signature without re-checking expiry or epoch fields.

evidence: Current mainnet.json omits the Civilization program ID; this is client configuration, not an on-chain disable switch

seedEvidence.title: Follow each public account back to the exact seed family that creates it.
seedEvidence.body: These graphs turn the Rust and SDK seed constants into a reviewer-facing evidence map, so drift in PDA names, signer boundaries, or runtime assumptions is easy to spot.

diagrams.title: Terrain writes stay anchored to GlobalConfig, not to a private map server.
diagrams.body: The world layer derives generated terrain from GlobalConfig, then records only sparse public evidence for broken blocks, foundation occupancy, resource drops, decoration rules, and player progress.

nodes.label: GlobalConfig
nodes.detail: The one-time config account storing world seed, dimensions, mint data, and hashes under current Core program logic.

nodes.label: mainnet.json
nodes.detail: The browser runtime chooses cluster and program IDs from this public file before reading PDAs.

nodes.label: ChunkBrokenState
nodes.detail: Stores compact 3-byte records for mined blocks inside one chunk.

nodes.label: FoundationChunk
nodes.detail: Indexes which foundations occupy a chunk so build and mining checks share a public conflict witness.

nodes.label: ResourceDropTable
nodes.detail: A global-config-scoped extra-drop rule table. The current seed is resource-drops-v2 and does not include a table ID.

nodes.label: SurfaceDecorationTable
nodes.detail: Publishes bounded surface decoration rules that the Chunk program can audit against generated terrain.

nodes.label: PlayerProgress
nodes.detail: Tracks per-owner progress under the program that awards the action, scoped by GlobalConfig.

evidence: resource-drops-v2 verified in Rust and SDK

diagrams.title: Wallet identity, sessions, equipment, and backpacks are separate evidence families.
diagrams.body: The player layer records profile/session relationships and Backpack owns slot state. Program PDA paths are scoped, but a BREAK_BLOCK session can also remove any selected Backpack slot through tag 2.

nodes.label: Owner wallet
nodes.detail: Funds and signs profile, backpack, market, equipment, and allowed action setup.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Submits action-mask-approved calls until a caller-chosen expiry; no maximum duration, revoke, or consumed counter is enforced.

nodes.label: PlayerProfile
nodes.detail: Stores owner, position, equipment pointers, equipped backpack, and update slots.

nodes.label: PlayerSession
nodes.detail: Binds owner and session authority with action mask, expiry, and stored maxActions/actionCount fields that current consumers do not enforce.

nodes.label: Appearance / Equipment
nodes.detail: Keeps appearance code and equipment slot state separate from the profile account.

nodes.label: Backpack
nodes.detail: Stores fixed 80-byte slots for block resources, materials, forged items, and escrow return paths.

nodes.label: BlueprintItem
nodes.detail: Records unique issuance and the initial recipient. Marketplace moves the Backpack slot but does not update this account's owner field.

nodes.label: Equipment transfer authority
nodes.detail: Lets the Player and Backpack programs move a custodied equipment slot without giving arbitrary write access.

nodes.label: Name / invite indexes
nodes.detail: Reserve canonical player names and invite pages without overloading the profile PDA.

evidence: Profile is not the inventory store
Session does not replace owner custody
Blueprint identity is unique, but its stored owner can become stale after marketplace delivery

diagrams.title: Cross-program mutations use explicit signer PDAs and public receipt records.
diagrams.body: Building, smelting, market, Guardian, and Civilization paths can be reviewed by tracing which PDA signs the CPI and which account becomes the durable evidence record.

nodes.label: BuildSite
nodes.detail: Stores foundation ownership, footprint, staged resize state, and active/pending revisions.

nodes.label: BuildingManifest / Shard
nodes.detail: Commits expected payload hash, shard bitmap, dimensions, offsets, and bounded upload payload.

nodes.label: Chunk authority
nodes.detail: Building signs chunk occupancy registration without becoming the Chunk program owner.

nodes.label: Guardian blueprint authority
nodes.detail: Building publishes restricted-wallet-supplied blueprint metadata through a scoped signer without checking a BuildingManifest.

nodes.label: Smelting / Market authorities
nodes.detail: Manufacturing and settlement append or restore Backpack slots only through their own signer PDA.

nodes.label: RecipeTable
nodes.detail: Stores recipes and authority for any unused table ID initialized by any signer; the seed does not identify a canonical table.

nodes.label: MarketplaceListing
nodes.detail: Escrows the full Backpack slot snapshot and records seller, buyer, currency, fee, and final state.

nodes.label: GuardianRegistry / Region
nodes.detail: Stores registry, treasury signer, region owner/operator, endpoint, stake, blueprint metadata, and dormant proof fields; no live proof or settlement instruction updates those fields.

nodes.label: Civilization rule records
nodes.detail: Splits proposals, signatures, caller-supplied tallies, execution receipts, power snapshots, and citizen power into separate PDAs; current client config does not determine on-chain callability.

instructionSurface.title: Trace every accepted instruction tag to the gate that handles it.
instructionSurface.body: These maps mirror the current Rust process_instruction match arms, including retired and invalid tags, so SDK builders and reviewers can spot stale integration assumptions before they reach chain calls.

diagrams.title: One namespace byte selects a compiled child processor without changing the incoming program ID.
diagrams.body: Calls to nicechunk_game use [namespace, childTag, childPayload...]. The router removes only the namespace byte, then passes the original accounts and incoming Game program ID to the selected child logic. Unified child PDA checks therefore derive under the Game executable ID. In the current mainnet.json, Backpack, Market, and Smelting use that route while Chunk remains standalone.

nodes.label: Game instruction data
nodes.detail: The first byte is the namespace. The next byte is the selected child's own instruction tag, followed by that child's payload bytes.

nodes.label: Incoming Game program ID
nodes.detail: The router forwards the same program_id reference instead of substituting the standalone child crate ID.

nodes.label: Namespace 1
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Backpack logic.

nodes.label: Namespace 2
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Chunk logic when Game is the addressed executable.

nodes.label: Namespace 3
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Smelting logic.

nodes.label: Namespace 4
nodes.detail: Routes the remaining child payload to Market logic.

nodes.label: Backpack processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 1 has been removed.

nodes.label: Chunk processor
nodes.detail: Can run inside Game through namespace 2, although the current client config addresses the standalone Chunk program.

nodes.label: Smelting processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 3 has been removed.

nodes.label: Market processor
nodes.detail: Reads the child tag after namespace 4 has been removed.

nodes.label: Unified PDA domain
nodes.detail: Account ownership and PDA derivation performed by routed child logic use the incoming Game program ID, not the standalone child ID.

nodes.label: Current client aliases
nodes.detail: backpack, market, and smelting currently resolve to the Game executable. Equal configured IDs are routing aliases, not proof of independent deployments.

nodes.label: Current Chunk route
nodes.detail: The current client addresses Chunk directly, so those calls use [childTag, childPayload...] and the standalone Chunk program ID rather than namespace 2.

evidence: The incoming Game program ID governs routed child PDA derivation
Current client config aliases Backpack, Market, and Smelting; Chunk remains standalone

diagrams.title: Identity and action authority are separated before gameplay writes.
diagrams.body: The current Core dispatcher accepts only the genesis initializer, while deployed upgrade authority remains separate evidence. Player tags include expiry-bearing sessions with caller-chosen duration, no revoke path, and non-consumed counter fields.

nodes.label: Core [0]
nodes.detail: initialize_global_config is the only accepted Core payload and anchors the world seed, mint, hashes, and runtime limits.

nodes.label: Player [0,7,8,9,10,11]
nodes.detail: Creates the profile, reserves names, stores appearance, and appends invite registration pages under owner-controlled indexes.

nodes.label: Player [1,4,5,6]
nodes.detail: Position, session refresh, equipped backpack, and forging XP are signer-gated; session counters are not consumed by current validators.

nodes.label: Player [2,12,13,14,15]
nodes.detail: Legacy and v2 equipment writes, cross-program slot transfers, swaps, and durability consumption stay in the Player equipment branch.

nodes.label: Profile / Session
nodes.detail: Profile proves owner identity while session proves signer/action-mask/expiry delegation; it does not enforce its stored action counter.

nodes.label: Equipment / Name / Invite
nodes.detail: Separate PDA families make display names, invite pages, and equipment slots auditable without overloading the profile account.

evidence: Session does not replace owner custody
Name and invite indexes are explicit

diagrams.title: World mutations run through generated-terrain checks and build-manifest gates.
diagrams.body: Chunk tags now start at the active mining and rule-table surface, while Building owns foundations, NCM3 shard uploads, chunk occupancy registration, and Guardian blueprint publishing.

nodes.label: Chunk [5,8,9,20,21]
nodes.detail: Single, rewarded, tree, batch, and range mining recompute generated blocks and write sparse broken-block evidence.

nodes.label: Chunk [6,15]
nodes.detail: Initializes chunk-broken storage and lets Building register occupied build-site chunks through a scoped authority.

nodes.label: Chunk [7,10,11,12,13]
nodes.detail: Resource drops, surface decoration, verifier checks, and Civilization receipts are separate rule or adapter branches.

nodes.label: Chunk [0-4]
nodes.detail: Legacy chunk initialization, delegation, and generated-block verifier tags are not accepted by the current dispatcher.

nodes.label: Building [0,1,6,7]
nodes.detail: Creates, indexes, migrates, and resizes BuildSite accounts after footprint and PlayerSession checks; the session check currently requests BREAK_BLOCK for every branch.

nodes.label: Building [2,3,4,5,8]
nodes.detail: Stages upload shards, finalizes hash-checked manifests, cancels uploads, and separately forwards restricted-wallet blueprint metadata without manifest verification.

nodes.label: Chunk / Build PDAs
nodes.detail: Broken blocks, occupied chunks, build sites, manifests, and shards are all public PDA evidence instead of private world state.

nodes.label: Guardian Blueprint
nodes.detail: The Building PDA signer updates Guardian region blueprint metadata only through the Guardian program gate.

diagrams.title: Backpack slot mutations include owner, session, and program-PDA branches.
diagrams.body: Smelting and Market use authority PDAs, while Backpack tag 2 also lets a BREAK_BLOCK session remove any selected slot. Smelting checks a selected table, not canonical provenance; tag 8 checks NCF1/materials, not BlueprintItem issuer evidence.

nodes.label: Backpack [0-6]
nodes.detail: Initializes backpacks and mutates slots; tag 2 permits either the owner or a BREAK_BLOCK session to remove any selected slot index.

nodes.label: Backpack [8-11]
nodes.detail: Tag 8 validates NCF1/material requirements but no BlueprintItem or issuer record. Tag 9 has a fixed issuer; Marketplace later moves its slot without updating BlueprintItem.owner.

nodes.label: Backpack [7]
nodes.detail: The unverified legacy forge instruction is deliberately disabled and returns UnverifiedForgeInstructionDisabled.

nodes.label: Smelting [0-4]
nodes.detail: Recipe table init, upsert, execute, authority transfer, and Civilization receipt application are all accepted branches.

nodes.label: Market [0,1,2]
nodes.detail: Create, cancel, and buy listing read or restore the full 80-byte Backpack slot snapshot through market authority.

nodes.label: Market [3]
nodes.detail: The legacy initialize_asset discriminator is disabled and returns InvalidInstruction.

nodes.label: Backpack / Recipe / Listing
nodes.detail: Slot bytes and settlement state are public, but RecipeTable provenance is external and BlueprintItem.owner can become stale after marketplace delivery.

nodes.label: Program authorities
nodes.detail: Smelting, Market, and equipment transfer authorities can mutate slots only through their own CPI boundaries.

Civilization implements tags 0-5, but its program ID is absent from current mainnet.json; that is a client configuration fact, not an on-chain gate.

nodes.label: Guardian [5,6,8]

nodes.label: Guardian [3,4]

cpiAuthority.title: Audit game-facing cross-program writes by caller, callee tag, signer PDA, and public evidence.
cpiAuthority.body: These maps follow the current NiceChunk invoke and invoke_signed sites in Rust, so reviewers can see exactly which program is allowed to mutate another program's state and which PDA proves the write.

diagrams.title: Building and Chunk writes cross program boundaries only through scoped PDA signers.
diagrams.body: The world layer has three sensitive CPI paths: Building indexes occupied chunks into Chunk, Building forwards restricted-wallet-supplied blueprint metadata to Guardian without manifest verification, and Chunk delivers mined resources after generated-terrain checks.

nodes.label: Building [1]
nodes.detail: Validates BuildSite and CPI accounts; its PlayerSession check currently requests BREAK_BLOCK rather than a distinct build permission.

nodes.label: Building [8]
nodes.detail: Restricts the publisher wallet, validates GlobalConfig, and signs a Guardian update with the blueprint authority PDA.

nodes.label: Chunk [8/9/20/21]
nodes.detail: These reward branches recompute generated blocks, write broken-block evidence, then append one or many Backpack resource slots. Tag 5 records the break only and performs no Backpack CPI.

nodes.label: Chunk [15]
nodes.detail: Accepts only the Building chunk-authority signer and writes FoundationChunk occupancy records.

nodes.label: Guardian [6]
nodes.detail: Updates blueprint hash, revision, and record count on a GuardianRegion through the Building PDA signer.

nodes.label: Backpack [1/6]
nodes.detail: Accepts ChunkBrokenState as signer evidence for single or batched mined resource delivery.

nodes.label: ChunkAuthority
nodes.detail: Derived by Building as ["chunk-authority-v1", globalConfig] and re-derived by Chunk under the Building program ID.

nodes.label: GuardianBlueprintAuthority
nodes.detail: Derived by Building as ["guardian-blueprint", globalConfig] and accepted by Guardian for blueprint-only mutation.

nodes.label: ChunkBrokenState
nodes.detail: The same account that records broken blocks signs Backpack delivery for the exact chunk coordinates.

nodes.label: FoundationChunk
nodes.detail: Chunk-scoped public index proving which foundation occupies each affected chunk.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion blueprint fields

nodes.label: Backpack resource slots

diagrams.body: Equipment, smelting, and marketplace CPIs use explicit tags and PDA signers, but direct Backpack tag 2 also accepts a BREAK_BLOCK session for arbitrary selected-slot removal. Listing evidence tracks slot bytes, not BlueprintItem.owner.

nodes.label: Player [13]

nodes.label: Smelting [2]

nodes.label: Market [0/1/2]

nodes.label: Backpack [10/11]

nodes.label: Backpack [4/5]
nodes.detail: Tag 4 removes selected inputs and fuel with owner consent; tag 5 appends normalized outputs with smelting-authority.

nodes.label: Backpack [2/3]
nodes.detail: Tag 2 removes the seller source slot; tag 3 restores or delivers the Listing-owned 80-byte slot with market-authority.

nodes.label: Player [2]

nodes.label: EquipmentTransferAuthority

nodes.label: SmeltingAuthority
nodes.detail: Derived under Smelting and limited to append_smelting_item, but that gate proves only a match to the selected program-owned RecipeTable, not trusted provenance.

nodes.detail: Required on the depicted smelting and market branches; direct Backpack tag 2 alternatively accepts a BREAK_BLOCK session for destructive removal.

nodes.label: Backpack slots

diagrams.title: Target-scoped adapters can execute a stored Civilization threshold result.
diagrams.body: Chunk and Smelting derive target-scoped adapter PDAs from a RuleBook. This prevents a generic target write, but the receipt may still rest on a 1 bps author-selected threshold, a finalizer-selected signature subset, and no enforced voting window.

nodes.label: Chunk [10/13]
nodes.detail: Applies resource-drop or surface-decoration Civilization receipts after validating the canonical Civilization program.

nodes.label: Smelting [4]
nodes.detail: Applies a Civilization recipe receipt before updating recipe authority-controlled state.

accountLifecycle.title: Follow PDA state from rent funding to migration, growth, closure, or durable settlement.
accountLifecycle.body: These maps explain how current contracts handle pre-funded PDAs, rent top-ups, realloc growth, legacy migration, and refund paths without turning transient accounts into invisible state.

diagrams.title: PDA birth paths diverge: some adopt pre-funded system accounts, while others require pristine targets.
diagrams.body: Selected Core, Player, Guardian, Chunk, and player-progress helpers explicitly top up, allocate, and assign a system-owned PDA that already holds lamports. Backpack, RecipeTable, Listing, Civilization, and Building creation paths shown here rely on create_account and do not provide that dust-adoption branch. Every path still needs the expected seed, owner, length, and rent evidence.

nodes.label: Payer / owner / session authority
nodes.detail: Funds rent and must satisfy the program-specific owner, session, treasury, or seller authority checks before a PDA is created.

nodes.label: find_program_address
nodes.detail: The program re-derives the expected PDA before any create, allocate, assign, or write step.

nodes.label: Rent minimum
nodes.detail: The target length is converted into rent-exempt lamports before funding or top-up.

nodes.label: Empty PDA
nodes.detail: Creates the PDA with system create_account and the program-derived signer seeds.

nodes.label: Explicitly supported pre-funded PDA
nodes.detail: Only helpers with an explicit branch top up the rent delta, then invoke allocate and assign for a system-owned zero-data PDA.
nodes.evidence: Core / Player / Guardian / Chunk / player-progress helpers

nodes.label: Create-account-only target
nodes.detail: Backpack, RecipeTable, Listing, Civilization, and Building main creation helpers call create_account without a transfer/allocate/assign fallback; a dusted address is not handled by those paths.

nodes.label: Program-owned PDA
nodes.detail: The final account is owned by the expected program and packed with the current magic, version, owner, and GlobalConfig fields.

nodes.label: Lifecycle audit proof
nodes.detail: A reviewer can compare seed family, owner, data length, magic bytes, bump, and updated slot to verify the account birth path.
nodes.evidence: RPC account owner + data length + decoder

Only explicit branches transfer the rent delta before allocate and assign

diagrams.title: Growing accounts preserve old evidence before they expose a larger current layout.
diagrams.body: Current code has several non-trivial migrations: ChunkBroken grows by capacity, FoundationChunk migrates v1 records to v2, Player accounts are upgraded to current lengths, and Building migrates legacy Chunk-owned build sites into Building-owned BuildSite v2 accounts.

nodes.label: ChunkBrokenState
nodes.detail: Starts with an initial record capacity and grows when single, batch, or range mining needs more room.

nodes.label: FoundationChunk v1
nodes.detail: Older chunk occupancy records are decoded, converted to v2, and filtered when a replacement supersedes them.

nodes.label: Player layout drift
nodes.detail: Player profile, equipment, and appearance accounts can be topped up and reallocated to current lengths.

nodes.label: Legacy BuildSite
nodes.detail: A Chunk-owned legacy build site is decoded and re-packed into the Building program BuildSite v2 PDA.

nodes.label: fund_account_to_rent_exempt + realloc
nodes.detail: The payer funds the rent delta before reallocation so the larger account remains rent-exempt.

nodes.label: Convert and preserve records
nodes.detail: Legacy records are migrated into the larger layout instead of being dropped during the version change.

nodes.label: BuildSite resize staging
nodes.detail: Resize checks active building fit, stores staged dimensions, then chunk indexing catches up through Building tag 1.

nodes.label: Fit and version proof
nodes.detail: Growth is bounded by max capacity, world height, footprint, active revision, and matching GlobalConfig.

nodes.label: Current PDA layout
nodes.detail: The resulting state is still public and decodable as ChunkBroken, FoundationChunk v2, Player current layout, or BuildSite v2.

evidence: FoundationChunk v1 records survive v2 migration
Player current layout upgrades are rent-funded
BuildSite resize is staged, not an unchecked overwrite

diagrams.title: Temporary accounts either refund rent on cancellation or stay as durable sold-state evidence.
diagrams.body: Not every terminal action means the same lifecycle result. Appearance closure, building upload cancellation, and market cancellation reclaim lamports; marketplace purchase keeps the sold listing as settlement evidence.

nodes.label: Player [9]
nodes.detail: Only the treasury authority can close a PlayerAppearance PDA and receive its lamports.

nodes.label: Building [5]
nodes.detail: Cancels an uploading revision, zeroes and closes program-owned shard accounts, and closes the manifest.

nodes.label: Market [1]
nodes.detail: Restores the escrowed Backpack slot, clears listing data, and refunds listing lamports to the seller.

nodes.label: Market [2]
nodes.detail: Transfers payment, delivers the slot bytes to the buyer, and marks the listing sold without closing it; a referenced BlueprintItem.owner is unchanged.

nodes.label: Treasury authority
nodes.detail: Appearance close requires the recipient to be the treasury authority signer.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Building upload cancellation returns manifest and shard lamports to the session authority account.

nodes.label: Seller
nodes.detail: Cancel refunds listing rent to the seller; purchase pays seller proceeds and leaves sold-state evidence.

nodes.label: Zeroed closed account
nodes.detail: Closed Appearance, canceled Building upload artifacts, and canceled Listings are zeroed and no longer durable semantic records.

nodes.label: Sold listing record
nodes.detail: A purchased listing remains as a program-owned settlement record with buyer, sold slot, and sold time fields.

nodes.label: Restored or delivered Backpack slot
nodes.detail: Cancel restores slot bytes to the seller Backpack; purchase delivers them to the buyer Backpack through market-authority. Neither path updates a referenced BlueprintItem.owner.

nodes.label: Terminal-state audit
nodes.detail: Reviewers should distinguish canceled-and-closed accounts from sold records that intentionally remain decodable.
