Purchased listings remain durable sold records
Building cancel refunds upload artifact rent

payloadTruth.title: Separate user-supplied bytes from facts recomputed from PDAs, hashes, recipes, and rule evidence.
payloadTruth.body: These maps show which payload fields are accepted as selectors or intent, and which item, building, recipe, identity, endpoint, and governance facts are re-derived from contract-owned evidence before state changes.

diagrams.title: Marketplace listings use 19 bytes of intent, then escrow exact Backpack slot bytes.
diagrams.body: Item fields come from the seller's Backpack slot rather than listing payload. This proves slot-byte provenance only: purchase does not update the owner stored in a referenced BlueprintItem account.

nodes.label: Seller signer
nodes.detail: The seller must sign and match the Backpack owner or equipped PlayerProfile owner before the listing is accepted.

nodes.label: CreateListingArgs
nodes.detail: Only listing_id, currency, source_type, source_index, and price_base_units are parsed from the user payload.

nodes.label: Backpack / profile gate
nodes.detail: Market re-checks Backpack magic, v3 owner, capacity, item count, PDA seed, and optional PlayerProfile equipment identity.

nodes.label: Slot lookup
nodes.detail: The selected Backpack slot must be a block or item record with nonzero quantity before it can be escrowed; block volume may still be zero.

nodes.label: Backpack v3 slot
nodes.detail: The source slot supplies the actual material, item PDA, coordinates, metadata, durability, and volume used by the listing.

nodes.label: Listing source_slot
nodes.detail: ListingAccount stores the full source slot bytes, so later cancel or purchase does not re-trust a new payload.

nodes.label: Cancel or buy
nodes.detail: Cancel or buy restores/delivers the same slot bytes and records settlement; a referenced BlueprintItem.owner is not changed.

diagrams.title: Uploaded building bytes become state only after shard completeness, hash, NCM3 parsing, and fit checks pass.
diagrams.body: The Building program accepts an expected hash, declared length, revision, rotation, offsets, and bounded shard writes. Finalization reconstructs the shard payload and re-computes every building fact that matters before activating a manifest.

nodes.label: BeginBuildingArgs
nodes.detail: Foundation ID, revision, quarter turns, payload length, expected hash, and optional X/Z offsets declare the upload target.

nodes.label: WriteBuildingShardArgs
nodes.detail: Each write names foundation, revision, shard index, offset, and bytes; oversized write payloads are rejected before storage.

nodes.label: BuildingManifest
nodes.detail: The manifest stores payload length, expected hash, shard count, rotation, offsets, and upload bitmap.

nodes.label: BuildingShard PDAs
nodes.detail: Shard accounts are tied to GlobalConfig, foundation ID, revision, shard index, uploaded length, and expected per-shard length.

nodes.label: Payload hash
nodes.detail: Finalize gathers every uploaded shard and rejects the manifest if hash_payload_slices does not match expected_hash.

nodes.label: NCM3 parser
nodes.detail: The parser requires NCM3 version 1, dimensions from 1 to 256, and at most 4,096 commands before deriving footprint height and width.

nodes.label: BuildSite fit check
nodes.detail: The derived NCM3 footprint must fit the BuildSite and world height after rotation and offsets; user bytes never set active dimensions directly.

nodes.label: Active revision
nodes.detail: Only a finalized manifest and BuildSite revision update represent durable building state; canceled uploads close transient shard evidence.

diagrams.title: Smelting and Civilization expose selected tables and supplied evidence, with provenance limits.
diagrams.body: Program-owned data is decodable but not automatically authoritative: any signer can create a RecipeTable, while a Civilization finalizer supplies the signature subset and no voting window is enforced.

nodes.label: Smelting execution payload
nodes.detail: The owner supplies recipe_id, input indexes, fuel indexes, and optional multiplier; the payload does not create output identity by itself.

nodes.label: RuleBook payload
nodes.detail: PublishRuleBookArgs stores hash commitments, target program, target PDA, total active power, threshold, target status, and risk.

nodes.label: RecipeTable
nodes.detail: RecipeRecord defines IO and yield inside a selected table; any signer may initialize an unused table ID, and no canonical table or authority is enforced.

nodes.label: RuleBook
nodes.detail: RuleBook is a public target-bound commitment with an author-selected threshold as low as 1 bps; it has no voting-expiry field.

nodes.label: Backpack input validation
nodes.detail: The program reads owner-validated Backpack slots and matches them against the caller-selected RecipeTable before removal; it does not validate table provenance.

nodes.label: Signature and tally checks
nodes.detail: Signatures bind side and settled power; finalization rejects duplicates and impossible sums only among accounts supplied by the finalizer, without a Clock-enforced window or completeness check.

nodes.label: Selected-table smelting output
nodes.detail: Output volume is calculated from the selected table and inputs before SmeltingAuthority appends slots; this does not make the table canonical.

nodes.label: ExecutionReceipt
nodes.detail: Execution requires the stored thresholdMet result and target adapter, but threshold may be 1 bps and the tally may omit available signatures with no enforced voting window.

diagrams.title: Player fields and Guardian metadata pass distinct gates; a Guardian blueprint summary is not checked against a BuildingManifest.
diagrams.body: Player names and model codes have their own bounds, and Guardian endpoint writes have role and format checks. Guardian blueprint metadata is authority-gated, but the Building tag-8 path forwards the supplied summary without reading or verifying a finalized BuildingManifest.

nodes.label: Name and appearance payloads
nodes.detail: Player names are bounded and canonicalized for username PDA hashing; appearance titles and NCM model code lengths are checked.

nodes.label: Guardian endpoint payload
nodes.detail: Endpoint updates parse host length, port, and TLS flag, then reject empty hosts, oversized hosts, invalid characters, and port zero.

nodes.label: Player canonical gate
nodes.detail: Profile writes require the player authority and the expected PlayerProfile, UsernameIndex, Appearance, or Equipment PDA.

nodes.label: Guardian role gate
nodes.detail: Endpoint changes require the region operator signer; blueprint changes require the Building-derived guardian-blueprint PDA authority, but that authority check does not bind the summary to a BuildingManifest.

nodes.label: Player public records
nodes.detail: UsernameIndex stores the canonical name hash, Appearance stores display metadata, and PlayerEquipment embeds verified Backpack records plus model hashes.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion
nodes.detail: GuardianRegion stores region coordinates, operator, endpoint, blueprint hash, revision, record count, and update slots.

nodes.label: Metadata truth check
nodes.detail: Reviewers can compare payload limits, authority signer, PDA seed, stored hash, and decoded record owner, but must not treat Guardian blueprint metadata as manifest-verified.

valueSettlement.title: Trace real token and lamport movement separately from item custody, rent, and governance evidence.
valueSettlement.body: These maps show where SOL or NCK actually moves, where rent is only funding PDA storage, and where gameplay evidence changes state without becoming a payment rail.

diagrams.title: A purchase moves SOL or NCK, delivers the escrowed Backpack slot bytes, and marks the listing sold without changing BlueprintItem.owner.
diagrams.body: Market purchase is the only current player-facing sale path with direct payment settlement. It validates the active listing, seller, currency, price, and source slot before splitting payment and delivering the escrowed slot snapshot; this is slot-byte movement, not transfer of a separate BlueprintItem owner field.

nodes.label: Active ListingAccount
nodes.detail: The listing PDA must be active, writable, program-owned, seller-bound, and derived from [listing, seller, listing_id].

nodes.label: Escrowed source_slot
nodes.detail: Payment settlement does not invent item data; it reads the stored Backpack slot snapshot from the listing.

nodes.label: purchase_listing router
nodes.detail: The account list length and payment path depend on whether the listing currency is SOL or NCK.

nodes.label: 1% fee calculation
nodes.detail: split_market_payment computes fee = price * 100 / 10,000 and seller_amount = price - fee with checked arithmetic.

nodes.label: SOL transfer path
nodes.detail: For SOL listings, the buyer signs system transfers to the seller and MARKET_TREASURY after the treasury address is pinned.

nodes.label: NCK transfer path
nodes.detail: For NCK listings, token accounts must match spl-token ownership, NCK_MINT, and buyer/seller/treasury owners before checked transfers run.

nodes.label: MarketAuthority delivery
nodes.detail: After payment, MarketAuthority appends the stored slot snapshot to the buyer Backpack; a referenced BlueprintItem.owner remains unchanged.

nodes.label: Sold listing record
nodes.detail: The listing is marked sold with buyer, slot, and timestamp instead of being closed, so settlement remains decodable.

diagrams.title: Rent movement funds PDA storage; only explicit close paths return lamports to an authorized recipient.
diagrams.body: Rent funding appears across many programs, but it is not protocol revenue. Reviewers should separate rent top-ups and realloc funding from terminal refunds and durable accounts intentionally kept for evidence.

nodes.label: Payer / owner / session authority
nodes.detail: Initial account creation and rent top-ups are funded by the instruction payer, owner, seller, session authority, or treasury authority depending on the program.

nodes.label: Rent minimum
nodes.detail: Programs call Rent::minimum_balance for the exact target length before create, top-up, allocate, assign, or realloc.

nodes.label: Create or explicitly supported top-up
nodes.detail: Empty targets use create_account. Only helper-specific Core, Player, Guardian, Chunk, and player-progress paths adopt a pre-funded system account with transfer, allocate, and assign; create-account-only paths do not.

nodes.label: Realloc growth
nodes.detail: ChunkBroken/FoundationChunk and the supported Player profile, equipment, and appearance upgrades top up rent before reallocating larger account layouts; Smelting, Guardian, and Building do not expose a comparable generic realloc-growth path.

nodes.label: Listing cancel refund
nodes.detail: Cancel restores the escrowed Backpack slot, zeroes listing data, and transfers listing lamports back to the seller.

nodes.label: Building upload cancel
nodes.detail: Canceling a building upload closes manifest and shard accounts to the session authority after BuildSite pending revision is cleared.

nodes.label: Appearance close
nodes.detail: PlayerAppearance close requires the configured treasury authority signer and returns lamports only to that same recipient.

nodes.label: Durable sold / proof records
nodes.detail: Sold listings, rule receipts, and long-lived evidence accounts remain decodable instead of being treated as refundable protocol funds.

diagrams.title: Guardian V2 registration transfers NCK into treasury custody with no deregistration, withdrawal, refund, reclaim, or slash path.
diagrams.body: Registry setup pins the treasury wallet, treasury authority PDA, treasury NCK token, NCK mint, and SPL Token program. Registration transfers the configured amount into treasury custody; the fixed treasury can replace an operator in one step, and V2 emits no structured lifecycle events.

nodes.label: Treasury wallet signer
nodes.detail: Registry initialization requires GUARDIAN_TREASURY_WALLET as signer and writable payer.

nodes.label: GuardianRegistry
nodes.detail: The registry stores GlobalConfig, NCK mint, treasury token, active count, stake amount, a dormant slash value, and genesis state.

nodes.label: Operator NCK token
nodes.detail: Registration validates the operator token account owner, NCK mint, operator signer, endpoint payload, and adjacency rule.

nodes.label: Treasury authority token
nodes.detail: Treasury token must be the registry token account owned by the derived guardian-treasury PDA authority.

nodes.label: Stake transfer_checked
nodes.detail: The SPL Token checked transfer moves GUARDIAN_STAKE_AMOUNT from operator token account to treasury token account.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion
nodes.detail: A region PDA is created or reactivated only after stake transfer, registry validation, operator signer checks, and endpoint bounds.

nodes.label: No V2 stake exit or slash path
nodes.detail: The slash amount remains encoded, but current V2 dispatch exposes no deregistration, withdrawal, refund, reclaim, or slash instruction.
nodes.evidence: retired proof/settlement tags; no stake lifecycle exit

nodes.label: Endpoint and operator updates
nodes.detail: The stored operator updates the endpoint, while the fixed treasury can replace the operator in one transaction without old- or new-operator acceptance; neither path moves NCK or lamports.

diagrams.title: Inventory, selected-recipe, mining, and proposal records can change state without moving SOL or NCK.
diagrams.body: Several high-value gameplay actions mutate PDA evidence or item custody, but they are not payment rails. Auditors should look for explicit system transfers or SPL Token transfers before classifying a path as value settlement.

nodes.label: Owner or session signer
nodes.detail: Mining and Building use session checks, while smelting and equipment use owner or program-specific signers. Civilization publication, tally finalization, and receipt execution accept any writable signer once referenced-state checks pass.

nodes.label: Program signer PDA
nodes.detail: Chunk, Smelting, Market, Player, and Building perform specific CPI writes through explicit PDA signers. Civilization records a receipt and validates a target-program-derived adapter signer supplied by the caller, but does not invoke the target program itself.

nodes.label: Backpack slot mutation
nodes.detail: Mined resources, smelting outputs, equipment transfers, and market deliveries change slot records rather than paying token balances.

nodes.label: Selected-table outputs
nodes.detail: Smelting matches Backpack inputs against the caller-selected program-owned RecipeTable and appends table-derived outputs through SmeltingAuthority. No SOL/NCK payment occurs, and the table is not thereby canonical or trusted.

nodes.label: Civilization power records
nodes.detail: Power snapshots, citizen power, signatures, tallies, and receipts store authority-settled power and a finalizer-supplied subset threshold result. They are not spendable NCK or proof of complete, windowed approval.

nodes.label: Building and chunk evidence
nodes.detail: BuildSite, BuildingManifest, BuildingShard, FoundationChunk, and ChunkBrokenState are public state proofs, not value escrows.

nodes.label: Value-path test
nodes.detail: Classify a branch as money movement only when it invokes system transfer, create-account rent funding, close/refund, or SPL Token transfer_checked.

authorityBoundary.title: Separate compile-time roots, human keys, scoped program signers, and limits the current code does not enforce.
authorityBoundary.body: This audit maps the authority checks present in the ten native NiceChunk program crates, including the unified namespace router. A compile-time key or one-time account is not, by itself, proof that an upgradeable deployment is immutable. None of the ten programs defines a custom msg!, sol_log, emit!, or event structure; audit evidence comes from account state, transaction history, CPIs, and transfers rather than an event stream.

diagrams.title: Core has no in-program admin or update path, while fixed treasury roles still depend on two human wallets.
diagrams.body: Core tag 0 writes a one-time GlobalConfig from constants and rejects every other tag. The other programs pin program IDs, mints, and role wallets in source, but source inspection cannot establish whether each deployed program's upgrade authority has been closed.

nodes.label: Core [0]
nodes.detail: Accepts only initialize_global_config. No admin account, pause, withdraw, or update-config instruction is present in the Core dispatch.

nodes.label: Ten program binaries
nodes.detail: Core, Player, Chunk, Unified Game, Backpack, Smelting, Market, Guardian, Civilization, and Building bind dispatch roots, trusted program IDs, or role keys through source code and compiled constants.

nodes.label: GlobalConfig
nodes.detail: The deterministic Core PDA is created once and stores fixed world, fee, supply, wallet, and rule-hash fields; Core exposes no instruction that rewrites them.

nodes.label: Cluster NCK mint
nodes.detail: Initialization pins the cluster mint and checks SPL Token ownership, 6 decimals, the fixed genesis supply, and absent mint and freeze authorities.

nodes.label: CtPV…7WvF
nodes.detail: CtPV2vmqNNwUSfMu5nz58ZtMPy6ZvxL4LyNdPHVW7WvF is compiled into Core, Player, and Market under three distinct roles.

nodes.label: 9Xuo…KVud

nodes.label: CtPV role cluster

diagrams.title: Sessions enforce identity, an action bit, and expiry; the stored action budget is not live.
diagrams.body: Player tag 4 requires both the owner wallet and temporary key to sign creation or refresh. Consumer programs read the session record, but current validators do not consume max_actions, increment action_count, or provide an owner-only revoke or close path.

nodes.label: Owner wallet
nodes.detail: Signs creation or refresh, funds the PDA, and is bound to the PlayerProfile and session seed family.

nodes.label: Session authority
nodes.detail: Co-signs tag 4 and later signs high-frequency actions against its owner-bound PlayerSession PDA.

nodes.label: Player [4]
nodes.detail: Accepts BREAK_BLOCK and PLACE_BLOCK mask bits, a future expires_at, and max_actions greater than zero; it does not cap how far in the future expiry may be.

nodes.label: PlayerSession
nodes.detail: Stores owner, temporary key, PlayerProfile, GlobalConfig, world, allowed_actions, expiry, max_actions, and action_count.

nodes.label: Player / Chunk / Backpack
nodes.detail: Their live session branches bind the temporary key to the stored profile or owner, reject expiry, and require the selected action bit before mutation.

nodes.label: Building player actions
nodes.detail: The shared Building validator passes action index 1 for every player action. That index is BREAK_BLOCK, while PLACE_BLOCK is index 2.

nodes.label: Identity + bit + expiry
nodes.detail: These are the effective on-chain session limits: account ownership and identity bindings, the requested action bit, and expires_at greater than the current time.

nodes.label: Action-count budget
nodes.detail: max_actions is written and action_count is reset to zero, but the audited validators neither compare the two fields nor increment action_count.

nodes.label: Revoke, close, duration cap
nodes.detail: Player exposes refresh with both signers, but no owner-only revoke, session close, or maximum-duration rule; expiry is the only automatic cutoff.

evidence: Tag 4 requires owner and session-authority signatures
Only BREAK_BLOCK and PLACE_BLOCK bits may be stored
max_actions and action_count do not bound live calls
Building requests action index 1, not PLACE_BLOCK index 2
No owner-only revoke, close, or maximum expiry duration exists

diagrams.title: Recipe, Guardian-operator, and blueprint paths use three different trust models.
diagrams.body: Smelting recipe tables are open to first initialization by table ID, Guardian operators are treasury-rotated, and blueprint publication or issuance uses fixed wallets and a Building PDA. The active Backpack forge path is separate from issued BlueprintItem evidence.

nodes.label: Open external signer
nodes.detail: Any signer may initialize an unused Smelting table_id and become its authority; a Backpack owner may separately invoke forge tag 8, which checks NCF1 bytes and materials but no BlueprintItem or issuer record.

nodes.label: Guardian treasury
nodes.detail: The fixed treasury signs Guardian tag 8 and can replace a region's stored operator in one transaction.

nodes.label: Current region operator
nodes.detail: The stored operator signs endpoint updates. Operator rotation does not require the old operator or the proposed new operator to sign.

nodes.label: Blueprint publisher keys
nodes.detail: Building accepts the treasury or configured publisher for Guardian metadata; Backpack tag 9 accepts only 9Xuo… as BlueprintItem issuer.

nodes.label: RecipeTable
nodes.detail: The initializing payer becomes authority. Tag 1 lets that authority upsert recipes; tag 3 writes a new authority key without new-authority acceptance and permits the default key.

nodes.label: GuardianRegion
nodes.detail: The owner field remains the fixed treasury, while operator, endpoint, and Guardian blueprint metadata occupy separate update branches.

nodes.label: GuardianBlueprintAuthority
nodes.detail: Building derives ["guardian-blueprint", GlobalConfig] and signs only the Guardian tag-6 blueprint metadata CPI.

nodes.label: Smelting [2]
nodes.detail: Execution requires a valid Smelting-owned RecipeTable but does not re-derive its table_id PDA or select a canonical table. Its smelting-authority PDA appends outputs to Backpack.

nodes.label: Backpack [9]
nodes.detail: The 9Xuo… issuer creates a unique BlueprintItem PDA and appends its item reference to the recipient's Backpack.

nodes.label: Backpack [8]
nodes.detail: Forge tag 8 checks the owner, NCF1-derived design requirements, and material inputs, but receives no BlueprintItem or fixed-issuer account.

evidence: Any unused recipe table_id may be initialized by its payer
Recipe authority transfer is one-step and accepts an unsigned new key
Guardian operator rotation is treasury-only and one-step
Guardian publication is PDA-scoped; Backpack issuance is fixed-issuer
Forge tag 8 does not consume or validate BlueprintItem evidence

diagrams.title: Civilization records a verifiable receipt chain, but its timing, threshold floor, and caller-selected tally set are material limits.
diagrams.body: The fixed power authority publishes snapshots and citizen allocations. Public callers may publish a RuleBook, finalize from the signature accounts they supply, and execute a passed receipt; actual rule mutation is implemented only by target-scoped Chunk and Smelting adapter paths in the audited code.

nodes.label: Power authority
nodes.detail: The fixed CIVILIZATION_POWER_AUTHORITY alone signs PowerSnapshot publication and CitizenPower settlement.

nodes.label: PowerSnapshot
nodes.detail: Commits total active power, epoch bounds, and optional expires_at under a snapshot hash.

nodes.label: CitizenPower
nodes.detail: Binds one citizen to a snapshot, exact power value, and inherited optional expiry before that citizen can create a RuleSignature.

nodes.label: Public payer / executor
nodes.detail: Any writable signer may fund RuleBook publication, tally finalization, or receipt execution once the referenced state passes validation.

nodes.label: RuleBook
nodes.detail: The author selects hashes, target program and PDA, target status, risk level, and threshold_bps from 1 through 10,000 against a valid snapshot.

nodes.label: RuleSignature set
nodes.detail: Each voter signs once with settled CitizenPower for the RuleBook snapshot and records agree, reject, abstain, or challenge power.

nodes.label: RuleTally
nodes.detail: Finalization iterates only the signature accounts supplied by its caller, rejects duplicate signers and aggregate power above total, then tests yes against required power and no.

nodes.label: ExecutionReceipt
nodes.detail: After a threshold-met tally, any executor may fund a one-time receipt; governable targets additionally require the target-derived adapter signer. The receipt records executor and time and is not a generic arbitrary-program mutation primitive.

nodes.label: Chunk / Smelting adapters
nodes.detail: Chunk tags 10/13 and Smelting tag 4 bind exact target program, target PDA, patch hash, tally, and receipt, then sign Civilization tag 3 with a target-derived adapter PDA.

nodes.label: Voting window and events
nodes.detail: Snapshot expiry is checked when nonzero during publication and signing, but RuleBook has no voting deadline and finalization has no time check. Civilization emits no program log events, so PDA state is the audit trail.

evidence: PowerSnapshot and CitizenPower require fixed 9Xuo… authority
Any payer may publish, finalize, and execute after state validation
The finalizer supplies the signature subset; duplicates and total-power overflow are rejected
Threshold accepts 1–10,000 bps and requires yes ≥ ceil(total × bps / 10,000) and yes > no
Only Chunk and Smelting expose audited mutation adapters; no RuleBook deadline or event stream exists
